title: Squared-logarithmic randomized k-server on arbitrary metrics

issues.description: Not a demonstrated error. On a fixed tau-separated tree, the allocation theorem combined with rounding (with the identity embedding, so P is about Q and no anchor travel) gives an O(log k)-competitive randomized k-server algorithm on tau-HSTs of arbitrary depth for an absolute tau. That improves the best known HST bound of O(log^2 k) (BCLLM18). The paper never states this corollary. I found nothing it contradicts: MTS on HSTs is O(log n), so the BCR Omega(log^2 k) instance cannot be a well-separated (k+1)-point HST. Still, it means Sections 3-5 carry a significant new result on their own and deserve the closest expert check.
issues.evidence: Theorem 3.1 gives V <= C_1*l*P + D_T for any fixed tree with tau >= tau_0, with no dependence on depth or degree. Prop 9.2 gives realization cost <= C(V + l*P + l*Q). The paper only cites BCLLM's O(log^2 k) for HSTs and does not remark on this improvement.

coverage: Read all ten sections in full. Checked the following line by line: lazy simulation (Lemma 2.1); the ball-mass telescope; the whole pilot-potential section (compactness, local structure, the deficit/displacement/slope bounds, the drift sum over scales including the moment and shell sums, the filtering corollary); heavy-ball edits and the annulus budget; the first-hit separation lemma and final-map separation; tier edits including the noncoverage table, retirement probabilities, the auxiliary short-roster potential and the insertion gain cases (heavy and nonheavy); the fixed-alphabet argument; rank-function identities and quotient bounds (verified by hand: A*t*^2 = 1 - 3p*, 2A*t* = 3, c't^2 = p*, -2c't + d't^2 = 1, quotient range [1/21, 0.82]); majorization superadditivity; the rank tracker (affine reference potential with bounded quadratic variation); the simplex and side trackers' feasibility exchange arguments; output feasibility under Rules I and II; switch hysteresis; star movement and the tree absorption; parked-coefficient telescope and retained-anchor potential; the balanced-rounding kernel exchange argument and tree matching; episode amplification, the finite minimax separation, Kuhn behavioral conversion, and the Tychonoff compactness and repeated-start step. Coarse-budget amortization (Lemma 3.6) and the adaptive-proportion accounting (Lemma 4.4) were checked at spot-check depth only; I did not re-derive every constant dependency.
main_claim: For every k >= 2, every metric space with at least k+1 points and every start configuration, randomized k-server against an oblivious adversary has competitive ratio O(log^2 k) with a single policy, and additive term B = 0 when the starting points are distinct. This matches the Bubeck-Coester-Rabani worst-case lower bound.
sibling_notes: No sibling entries existed for family 110 when I checked. The proof chain is P <= C*l*Q (online partitions paid by the pilot potential), then V <= C*l*P (posterior-rank tree allocation), then anchor travel and balanced rounding at O(1) loss, then a finite-law to single-policy transfer (episodes, minimax, Tychonoff). Each link checked out. The key device throughout: potentials affine in posterior quantities with held coefficients, so filtering costs nothing in expectation, plus hysteresis trackers whose resets are paid by bounded quadratic variation. Any companion paper that reuses these trackers or the pilot potential can rely on the versions here. The allocation theorem on its own implies O(log k) for k-server on tau-HSTs, which the paper does not state.
